book.name: The Tourney at Sallowfield
book.text: At Sallowfield, for Lady Day, Sir Guillaume Sallow carried the prize. He broke 4 lances and struck the helm once. The heralds gave him the prize for the most helm strikes of the day.

book.name: The Tourney at Hollin Moor
book.text: At Hollin Moor, for Eastertide, Sir Guillaume Sallow reached the last four before Sir Humphrey de Saint-Aubin put him out. He broke 3 lances and bore Sir Alain de Beaumaine to the ground. He was himself borne down by Sir Humphrey de Saint-Aubin. The heralds wrote well of his conduct. The prize went to Sir Jehan de Beaumaine.

book.name: The Duke of Aumbry’s Tourney
book.text: At Ambry Cross, for Whitsun, Sir Guillaume Sallow reached the last four before Sir Amaury Lacy put him out. He broke 2 lances. He was himself borne down by Sir Amaury Lacy. The prize went to Sir Amaury Lacy.

book.name: The joust on the green at Merrow
book.text: At Merrow, for Midsummer, Sir Guillaume Sallow rode to the last two, and was beaten there by Sir Humphrey Gournay. He broke 3 lances. He vowed to bear Sir Humphrey Gournay down, and did not. The heralds wrote that his conduct was wanting. The prize went to Sir Humphrey Gournay.

book.name: The Tourney at Othery
book.text: At Othery, for St James, Sir Guillaume Sallow rode in the first round and was put out by Sir Enguerrand Wyvenhoe. He broke no lance. He was himself borne down by Sir Enguerrand Wyvenhoe. The prize went to Sir Jehan Denholm.

book.name: The Earl of Stane’s Tourney
book.text: At Castle Brede, for Lammas, Sir Guillaume Sallow reached the last four before Sir Geoffrey Ashcombe put him out. He broke 1 lance and bore Sir Warin Quarles to the ground. He was himself borne down by Sir Geoffrey Ashcombe. The prize went to Sir Geoffrey Ashcombe.

book.name: The joust on the green at Sallowfield
book.text: At Sallowfield, for Lady Day, Sir Guillaume Sallow rode in the first round and was put out by Sir Aymer Challon. He broke 3 lances. He was himself borne down by Sir Aymer Challon. It was thought a small field for a knight of his name. The prize went to Sir Aymer Challon.

book.name: The Duke of Aumbry’s Tourney
book.text: At Ambry Cross, for Whitsun, Sir Guillaume Sallow rode in the first round and was put out by Sir Edmund Thorne. He broke no lance. He was himself borne down by Sir Edmund Thorne. The prize went to Sir Edmund Thorne.

book.name: The Tourney at Wystan’s Ford
book.text: At Wystan’s Ford, for St James, Sir Guillaume Sallow rode in the first round and was put out by Sir Humphrey Gournay. He broke 2 lances. He was himself borne down by Sir Humphrey Gournay. He was carried from the lists and the surgeon was sent for. The prize went to Sir Humphrey Mallory.

book.name: The Tourney at Othery
book.text: At Othery, for Lady Day, Sir Guillaume Sallow carried the prize. He broke 5 lances.

book.name: The Tourney at Sallowfield
book.text: At Sallowfield, for Eastertide, Sir Guillaume Sallow rode in the first round and was put out by Sir Osbert Aubrecy. He broke 1 lance and struck the helm once. The heralds gave him the prize for the most helm strikes of the day. The prize went to Sir Philippe Orme.

book.name: The Tourney at Merrow

book.name: The Duke of Aumbry’s Tourney
book.text: At Ambry Cross, for Whitsun, Sir Guillaume Sallow rode in the first round and was put out by Sir Humphrey Redvers. He broke 1 lance. The prize went to Sir Humphrey Redvers.

book.name: The Earl of Stane’s Tourney
book.text: At Castle Brede, for Lammas, Sir Guillaume Sallow rode to the last two, and was beaten there by Sir Osbert Aubrecy. He broke 6 lances and struck the helm once. The prize went to Sir Osbert Aubrecy.

book.name: The pas held by Sir Baudouin Corbet
book.text: On the road to Othery, Sir Guillaume Sallow touched the shield of Sir Baudouin Corbet at a bridge, and rode through. He broke 3 lances and struck the helm once.

book.name: The Tourney at Othery
book.text: At Othery, for Michaelmas, Sir Guillaume Sallow carried the prize. He broke 7 lances and struck the helm once. The heralds gave him the prize for the most helm strikes of the day.

book.name: The Tourney at Wystan’s Ford
book.text: At Wystan’s Ford, for St Luke, Sir Guillaume Sallow carried the prize. He broke 6 lances, struck the helm twice and bore Sir Bertrand Esterling to the ground.

book.name: The Tourney at Port Lessing
book.text: At Port Lessing, for Lady Day, Sir Guillaume Sallow carried the prize. He broke 4 lances, struck the helm once and bore Sir Thibaut Lacy to the ground. The heralds gave him the prize for the most helm strikes of the day. It was thought a small field for a knight of his name.

book.name: The Duke of Aumbry’s Tourney
book.text: At Ambry Cross, for Whitsun, Sir Guillaume Sallow reached the last four before Sir Edmund Thorne put him out. He broke 4 lances and struck the helm twice. He was himself borne down by Sir Edmund Thorne. The heralds gave him the prize for the most helm strikes of the day. The prize went to Sir Edmund Thorne.

book.name: The King’s Tourney at Midsummer
book.text: At Kingsmead, for Midsummer, Sir Guillaume Sallow reached the last four before Sir Humphrey Mallory put him out. He broke 4 lances and bore Sir Alain de Beaumaine to the ground. The prize went to Sir Humphrey Mallory.

book.name: The Earl of Stane’s Tourney
book.text: At Castle Brede, for Lammas, Sir Guillaume Sallow rode in the first round and was put out by Sir Humphrey Gournay. He broke 2 lances. The prize went to Sir Geoffrey Wyvenhoe.

book.name: The Tourney at Merrow
book.text: At Merrow, for Michaelmas, Sir Guillaume Sallow rode in the first round and was put out by Sir Richard Redvers. He broke no lance. It was thought a small field for a knight of his name. The prize went to Sir Baudouin Corbet.

book.name: The Tourney at Queenshythe
book.text: At Queenshythe, for St Luke, Sir Guillaume Sallow rode in the first round and was put out by Sir Walter Umfray. He broke no lance. It was thought a small field for a knight of his name. The prize went to Sir Walter Umfray.

book.name: A name
book.text: The heralds have begun to call him Sir Guillaume Sallow the Generous.

book.name: The Tourney at Fennick
book.text: At Fennick, for Lady Day, Sir Guillaume Sallow the Generous carried the prize. He broke 6 lances, struck the helm twice and bore Sir Warin Ashcombe to the ground. The heralds gave him the prize for the most helm strikes of the day. It was thought a small field for a knight of his name.

lastResult.prompt: The bishop has preached against the tourney from the cathedral steps, and says any who ride tomorrow ride in mortal sin.

lastResult.text: He absolves you, takes your shilling, and wishes you well in the lists.
